input.instruction: Explain why leaves look green to a curious eight-year-old.
input.response: Leaves are green because they contain chlorophyll, a pigment that absorbs red and blue wavelengths and reflects green wavelengths.
input.reference_answer: Leaves have a green substance called chlorophyll. It helps plants catch sunlight to make their food. Sunlight has many colors mixed together. The leaf uses mostly red and blue light, and bounces green light back to your eyes. That is why you see green!
